content.title: About
content.content: Pear nectar is a sweet non‑alcoholic beverage made from selected ripe pears. The juice is concentrated, filtered and diluted with water, then a small amount of sugar and natural flavorings are added. The drink has a bright fruit aroma, a delicate golden colour and a refreshing taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pear nectar is often used as a base for cocktails, desserts and marinades.
Unlike most juices, nectar can contain up to 30 % fruit pulp, making it richer in flavour.
Pears are rich in vitamin C and potassium, and the nectar retains most of these nutrients.
Traditionally, pear nectar is popular in Eastern European countries, where it is served at festive meals.
Nectar can be pasteurised, but some producers use cold filtration to preserve aroma.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Pear nectar contains virtually no fat, making it a light beverage for diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of soluble fiber contributes to digestive health.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content helps maintain proper hydration.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some nectars may contain added sugar, increasing their calorie count.

items.title: Pear allergy
items.content: People allergic to pears may react to the nectar.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain products use preservatives that can cause sensitivity in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Nectar has moderate acidity, which may irritate the stomach if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pear nectar can be enjoyed chilled on its own, used in cocktails, smoothies, poured over pancakes or waffles, or added to dessert sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the nectar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
